work: Audible Debate of Agents v1: text-ahead pipeline, per-performer model/effort/source, Line Machine voices, ready-to-use page
author: Jimmy in Claude Code (Opus 5.5), session 2026-11-14
_order: needs -> reality_gate.py freeze -> design (after freeze) -> independent R1 (r1_report + checked_at) -> build -> independent R2. Run reality_gate.py next REALITY.json

needs.verbatim: llm calls + TTS call + other parts of the project have their own time/latency that in summation it may make the performance slow and seeming interrupted. I suggest keeping the discussion between agent go through text sooner; even sooner than start of TTS ... the interface starts playing the debate later ... when it has a few voices to play ... and the performance goes on without interruption.
needs.situation: A listener (the owner in rehearsal, later an audience) hears the two performers speak in turn. Each turn's text comes from a free remote or local model (3-60 s) and then a voice engine (1-20 s).
needs.today: v0 is serial by design: turn N+1 is only requested after turn N has finished playing, so every model call plus synthesis is heard as dead air between turns (cloud packet REVIEW_PACKET.md; controller.py docstring 'v0 does NOT pre-generate').
needs.success_in_reality: After one announced pre-roll at the start, the listener hears turn after turn separated only by the designed gap; no turn waits on a model or a voice engine.
needs.probe: Run a 6-turn debate with a real free model and real Line Machine voices; read the per-turn undesigned wait (underrun) from the session metrics after the first turn.
needs.metric: max underrun after the first turn in seconds (target 0, accept <= 0.5); pre-roll length in seconds

needs.verbatim: use local machine capabilities + all our free sources of models -> selectable for agent with: model - effort - source
needs.situation: Preparing or rehearsing, the owner wants to try a different free model, source or thinking effort for performer A and for performer B, and compare, without editing code or typing commands.
needs.today: One --endpoint and one --model for both performers, typed on a command line; only LM Studio was considered and it is not running on this laptop; the machine's free gateways (Kilo free, OpenCode Zen free, Cline free via 9router) are unused.
needs.success_in_reality: On one page he picks, for A and for B separately, a source, a model from the live list of what that source actually offers for free right now, and an effort; the session record names exactly what each performer used, including the model actually served.
needs.probe: Open the page, choose two different sources for A and B, start, then open the session's config.json and turn records.
needs.metric: clicks to set both performers; number of live free sources and models listed; mismatch between chosen and recorded (target 0)

needs.situation: The performers should speak with voices the owner already has and knows: the Line Machine's Persian and English voices (local Piper, Windows, and its free cloud voices).
needs.today: The debate prototype has only silent placeholder audio and an untested Piper wrapper; the Line Machine already serves voices over /api/speak but the debate cannot reach it.
needs.success_in_reality: He picks a Line Machine voice for each performer; the debate speaks with those voices; each turn's length is measured from the real audio file and never exceeds the ceiling.
needs.probe: Start a session with two Line Machine voices; check each turn's WAV is real speech from Line Machine (engine field, non-silent samples) and duration_s <= ceiling via `verify`.
needs.metric: turns with real speech / total; turns over ceiling (target 0)

needs.verbatim: never claim the pilot works because two requests returned text or two WAVs were synthesized; a valid pilot needs human-controlled continuous two-way audition, timing enforcement, persistence, preserved evidence (owner stop condition, HANDOFF_JIMMY.md section 4.4)
needs.situation: With turns now prepared ahead, the operator presses Pause or Stop during speech or while text is still being written for later turns, on this Windows laptop.
needs.today: On Windows, Pause freezes the clock but not the sound (SIGSTOP does not exist); a text-ahead queue would also add the risk that queued turns keep sounding after Stop.
needs.success_in_reality: Pause silences the sound at once and nothing new is written or voiced while paused; Stop silences at once and no queued turn is ever heard afterwards; a restarted app never plays by itself; everything is saved.
needs.probe: Silent device test: play a silent WAV through the Windows player, pause, resume, stop, read device state and timing; controller tests with a full queue: stop and pause during speech and during generation.
needs.metric: stop-to-silence latency ms; turns heard after Stop (target 0); work done while paused (target 0)

needs.verbatim: make it finalize -> ready to be used
needs.situation: The owner is not technical, may be interrupted, and opens the work later alone.
needs.today: Running it needs git, PowerShell commands, flags and reading JSON.
needs.success_in_reality: He double-clicks one file, a page opens, he chooses performers and voices and presses Start; a short run-book tells him what he should hear and what to do if not.
needs.probe: A fresh reader follows only the run-book's first card from double-click to the first turn heard.
needs.metric: minutes to first heard turn; questions he had to ask (target 0)

N1.cut_for_words: nothing; lookahead=0/preroll=1 is a labelled v0 comparison
N1.evidence: R1_REPORT.md section N1; DESIGN.md Revision 3 item 1; round-2 deadlock closed
